stances.claim: When June 1991 arrived, Art did not speak of legacy -- he spoke of accounting; true to his nature, he refused to let the Rotary presidency dissolve into memory without measurement.
stances.rhetorical_move: not-legacy-but-accounting opening reframe + true-to-his-nature character framing + dissolve-into-memory-without-measurement institutional-discipline anchor

stances.claim: At his valedictory meeting he distributed a 94-page Final Report -- a document unprecedented in the history of the Rotary Club of Manila; it was exhaustive, almost severe in its precision; numbers were tallied, projects itemized, outcomes measured against promises; of the 178 projects pledged at the start of his term, 185 had been implemented; of the ₱90 million budget once deemed unrealistic, nearly all had been responsibly deployed; committees had multiplied, attendance had deepened, service had expanded beyond rhetoric into reach.
stances.rhetorical_move: 94-page-Final-Report unprecedented-credential + exhaustive-and-almost-severe-in-precision document-character + 185-of-178 overdelivery-specifically + budget-responsibly-deployed + four-fold institutional-improvement cascade (committees + attendance + service + reach)

stances.claim: But what mattered most was not arithmetic -- it was credibility; for the first time in years, Manila Rotary was being spoken of not merely as influential, but as effective; not merely prestigious, but purposeful; the Club had rediscovered its moral center without sacrificing its civic breadth.
stances.rhetorical_move: not-arithmetic-but-credibility reframe + not-merely-X-but-Y twin-rephrasing (influential→effective + prestigious→purposeful) + rediscovered-moral-center-without-sacrificing-civic-breadth balance closing

stances.claim: Art did not claim credit -- instead, he offered confession; in his closing address he described himself not as a successful leader but as an unworthy servant, sustained not by talent alone but by grace; it was an unsettling posture for an audience accustomed to triumphal retrospectives, yet it resonated; his humility did not diminish his authority -- it clarified it.
stances.rhetorical_move: did-not-claim-credit-offered-confession reframe + unworthy-servant-sustained-by-grace-not-talent self-characterization + unsettling-posture-yet-resonated + humility-did-not-diminish-authority-but-clarified-it titular maxim

stances.claim: Something had shifted -- men who had once regarded him as a capable lawyer now saw him as a trusted steward; business leaders observed how he balanced vision with discipline; clergy took note of a layman who understood that faith, to be credible, must translate into service; public officials, watchful and pragmatic, recognized in him a rare combination: decisiveness without arrogance, conviction without cruelty.

stances.claim: He had passed a test few recognized at the time -- not of popularity, but of governance.

one_paragraph_summary: Art's outgoing-Rotary-presidency chapter at the June 1991 valedictory, where he 'spoke not of legacy but of accounting,' distributing a 94-page Final Report 'unprecedented in the history of the Rotary Club of Manila' -- 'exhaustive, almost severe in its precision.' The numbers anchored the year: 185 implemented of 178 projects pledged, nearly all of the once-deemed-unrealistic ₱90M budget responsibly deployed, committees multiplied, attendance deepened, service 'expanded beyond rhetoric into reach.' But 'what mattered most was not arithmetic -- it was credibility'; 'for the first time in years, Manila Rotary was being spoken of not merely as influential, but as effective; not merely prestigious, but purposeful.' At the closing address he did not claim credit -- he offered confession, describing himself 'not as a successful leader, but as an unworthy servant, sustained not by talent alone but by grace.' The posture unsettled an audience accustomed to triumphal retrospectives, yet 'his humility did not diminish his authority -- it clarified it.' Something had shifted: 'men who had once regarded him as a capable lawyer now saw him as a trusted steward'; business leaders, clergy, and public officials began to recognize 'a rare combination: decisiveness without arrogance, conviction without cruelty.' Closing maxim: 'He had passed a test few recognized at the time -- not of popularity, but of governance.'
